title: Local and global maxima and minima
goal: Spot every place a peak or valley could hide: flat spots where $f'(c) = 0$ (critical points) and sharp corners where $f'(c)$ does not exist (singular points).

beforeThis.skill: Quick check: a local max/min is the highest/lowest point in its immediate neighbourhood; a global max/min is the champion across the entire domain.

questions.asking: Locate every point on the graph where the tangent is horizontal (critical point) or where the curve has a sharp corner (singular point), and state which ones are local extrema.
questions.statement: Identify every critical point and every singular point of $f(x)$ shown on the graph below. Which correspond to local extrema?

questions.asking: Find all critical points, singular points, local extrema, and global extrema over the plotted interval.
questions.statement: Identify every critical point and every singular point of $f(x)$ on the graph below. Which correspond to local extrema? Which correspond to global extrema over the interval shown?

questions.asking: Sketch a graph $y = f(x)$ that has a local peak at $x = 2$ but reaches even higher values elsewhere.
questions.statement: Draw a graph $y = f(x)$ where $f(2)$ is a local maximum, but it is not a global maximum.

questions.asking: Compute $f'(x)$ to find all critical points and singular points of $f(x) = \frac{x - 1}{x^2 + 3}$, and list all candidate $x$-values for local extrema.
questions.statement:
Suppose $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 1}{x^2 + 3}$.

  1. Find all critical points.
  2. Find all singular points.
  3. What are the possible points where local extrema of $f(x)$ may exist?

questions.asking: For each of the four graphs, state whether the value $f(2)$ at the filled dot is a local maximum, a local minimum, or neither.
questions.statement: Below are a number of curves, all of which have a singular point at $x = 2$. For each, label whether $x = 2$ is a local maximum, a local minimum, or neither.

figures.alt: Four small graphs each showing behavior at x = 2: first graph rises from the left to an open circle at x = 2 and has a higher filled dot at x = 2 with a line sloping down to the right; second graph rises from the left to a filled dot at x = 2 and jumps up to an open circle sloping down to the right; third graph rises from the left to an open circle at x = 2 and jumps up to a filled dot sloping up to the right; fourth graph is a V-shaped corner at x = 2 with an open circle at the bottom vertex and a filled dot floated higher above it.

questions.asking: Sketch a curve where $x = 2$ is an interior local maximum without $f'(2) = 0$ (so $f'(2)$ does not exist).
questions.statement: Draw a graph $y = f(x)$ where $f(2)$ is a local maximum, but $x = 2$ is not a critical point and is not an endpoint.

questions.asking: Find every $x$-value where $f'(x) = 0$ or where $f'(x)$ fails to exist for $f(x) = \sqrt{|(x - 5)(x + 7)|}$.
questions.statement:
$$f(x) = \sqrt{|(x - 5)(x + 7)|}$$

Find all critical points and all singular points of $f(x)$. You do not have to specify whether a point is critical or singular.

questions.asking: State the critical points, singular points, and local/global maxima and minima of the constant function $f(x) = 4$.
questions.statement: Suppose $f(x)$ is the constant function $f(x) = 4$. What are the critical points and singular points of $f(x)$? What are its local and global maxima and minima?
